build.note: Read from the saved raw capture with the L3207 cell reader and the EBX decoder; no export, no new capture.

question: What do stored blast damage, the material grid and the flak multipliers of L3315 give for explosive damage to a soldier?

sourceFacts.method: For each of 26 explosion objects the blast damage (registry default where a row exists, otherwise the asset's own value) and the explosion material were read, and Field_674633de for that material against the soldier materials 24, 25 and 26 of the hit-zone record. The product was multiplied by the three flak multipliers of L3315. EA's 1.3.1.0 and 1.3.3.0 statements about lethal radius and minimum explosive damage were compared with the registry radius rows.

control.description: EA: the aim-guided shell remains lethal within 2 m. Stored: blast damage 200, grid value 1, inner radius 1 m, radius 3 m; a straight-line falloff gives exactly 100 at 2 m. One control fits and one EA statement (HEAT-MP-T lethal radius 1.25 m) does not.

rawCheckSummary.tool: scripts/frosty-raw-check.py --manifest (stored values: raw-checks.json; grid reads: all-grid-rawchecks.json)

officialStatements.statement: Aim-Guided Shells: remains lethal against soldiers within 2m (1.3.1.0)
officialStatements.note: 200 x 1 falling in a straight line from the inner radius 1 m to 0 at the radius 3 m gives exactly 100 at 2 m. The straight-line falloff is an assumption.

officialStatements.statement: MBT 120mm HEAT-MP-T Rounds total blast radius increased from 4m to 5m, and lethal radius increased from 1m to 1.25m (1.3.3.0)
officialStatements.note: Registry BlastRadius 5 equals EA's total radius. Registry InnerBlastRadius is 1, not 1.25, and 100 x 1 is lethal only inside the inner radius, so EA's lethal radius 1.25 is not reproduced.

officialStatements.statement: Most land vehicle explosive weapons now have a minimum explosive damage of 20% (1.3.1.0)
officialStatements.note: Registry MinimumBlastDamage 20 against BlastDamage 100 for tank HE and HEAT-MP-T; whether the row is a percentage or a damage value is not separated by these two weapons.

inference: Explosions carry a damage value against the abdomen material only, so blast damage to a soldier is taken as blast damage x that value, the same for every body part.
Flak multipliers are applied as a further product (0.67, 0.75, 0.8). The stored values are not shown to be combined this way; this is the reading the field name supports (L3315).
The guided-shell statement supports blast damage x grid value with a falloff between the inner radius and the radius. The HEAT-MP-T lethal radius does not follow from the stored inner radius.
unresolved: No in-game reading. Test: stand 1 m from a C-4 pack with and without the Flak upgrade; death and 67 expected.
Stacking of flak effects. Test: Flak while prone; 50.25 from a full C-4 blast if multiplied.
Falloff shape. Test: tank HE at 3 m and 4 m from a soldier; about 78 and 49 on a straight line with the 20 minimum.
HEAT-MP-T lethal radius 1.25 m against the stored inner radius 1. Test: the shell at 1.1 m from a full-health soldier.
Radius rows for launchers and C-4 are not in the registry; the assets' own radius fields are not named.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Explosive damage to soldiers from the material grid and the flak multipliers
leads.summary: For 26 explosions the grid stores a damage value against the soldier abdomen material only (1 for shells, rockets, C-4 and mines; 0.85 for top-attack warheads; 0.8 for bombs; 0.6 for anti-air missiles; 0.4 for the SLAM body). Blast damage times that value, times the L3315 flak multipliers, is tabulated as a prediction. EA's guided-shell lethal distance of 2 m is reproduced; the HEAT-MP-T lethal radius is not. 13170 raw reads matched.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game blast damage reading on a soldier with and without flak.
leads.statusNote: Prediction from stored values; one EA statement fits, one does not; no in-game reading.
